cases.sentence: В одиночестве человек большею частью отдается ___, в обществе напротив — второму.
cases.explain: «первому голосу» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: With the enemy’s approach to Moscow, the Moscovites’ view of their situation did not grow more serious but on the contrary became even more frivolous, as always happens with people who see a great danger approaching. At the approach of danger there are always two voices that speak with equal power in the human soul: one very reasonably tells a man to consider the nature of the danger and the means of escaping it; the other, still more reasonably, says that it is too depressing and painful to think of the danger, since it is not in man’s power to foresee everything and avert the general course of events, and it is therefore better to disregard what is painful till it comes, and to think about what is pleasant. In solitude a man generally listens to the first voice, but in society to the second. So it was now with the inhabitants of Moscow. It was long since people had been as gay in Moscow as that year.

cases.sentence: — Вы никому не делаете милости, — сказала Жюли Друбецкая, собирая и прижимая кучку нащипанной корпии ___, покрытыми кольцами.
cases.explain: «тонкими пальцами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “You don’t spare anyone,” said Julie Drubetskáya as she collected and pressed together a bunch of raveled lint with her thin, beringed fingers.

cases.sentence: Жюли собиралась на ___ уезжать из Москвы и делала прощальный вечер.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Julie was preparing to leave Moscow next day and was giving a farewell soiree.

cases.sentence: Жюли собиралась на другой день уезжать из Москвы и делала ___.
cases.explain: «прощальный вечер» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Julie was preparing to leave Moscow next day and was giving a farewell soiree.

cases.sentence: — сказал ___ в ополченском мундире, которого Жюли называла: «mon chevalier»,[655] мой рыцарь, и который с нею вместе ехал в Нижний.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “A forfeit!” cried a young man in militia uniform whom Julie called “mon chevalier,” and who was going with her to Nízhni.

cases.sentence: — сказал молодой человек в ___, которого Жюли называла: «mon chevalier»,[655] мой рыцарь, и который с нею вместе ехал в Нижний.
cases.explain: «ополченском мундире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “A forfeit!” cried a young man in militia uniform whom Julie called “mon chevalier,” and who was going with her to Nízhni.

cases.sentence: В обществе Жюли, как и во многих обществах Москвы, было положено говорить только по-русски, и те, которые ошибались, говоря ___, платили штраф в пользу комитета пожертвований.
cases.explain: «французские слова» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: In Julie’s set, as in many other circles in Moscow, it had been agreed that they would speak nothing but Russian and that those who made a slip and spoke French should pay fines to the Committee of Voluntary Contributions.

cases.sentence: — ___ за галлицизм, — сказал русский писатель, бывший в гостиной.
cases.explain: «Другой штраф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Another forfeit for a Gallicism,” said a Russian writer who was present. “ ‘What pleasure is there to be’ is not Russian!” “You spare no one,” continued Julie to the young man without heeding the author’s remark.

cases.sentence: — Другой штраф за галлицизм, — сказал ___, бывший в гостиной.
cases.explain: «русский писатель» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Another forfeit for a Gallicism,” said a Russian writer who was present. “ ‘What pleasure is there to be’ is not Russian!” “You spare no one,” continued Julie to the young man without heeding the author’s remark.

cases.sentence: — Мы только говорили о вас, — с свойственною ___ свободой лжи, сказала Жюли.
cases.explain: «светским женщинам» — after the preposition «с», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “For caustique—I am guilty and will pay, and I am prepared to pay again for the pleasure of telling you the truth. For Gallicisms I won’t be responsible,” she remarked, turning to the author: “I have neither the money nor the time, like Prince Galítsyn, to engage a master to teach me Russian!” “Ah, here he is!” she added. “Quand on … No, no,” she said to the militia officer, “you won’t catch me. Speak of the sun and you see its rays!” and she smiled amiably at Pierre. “We were just talking of you,” she said with the facility in lying natural to a society woman. “We were saying that your regiment would be sure to be better than Mamónov’s.”

cases.sentence: — И он так бестолков — ___.
cases.explain: «сам граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I hear that their affairs are in a very bad way,” said Julie. “And he is so unreasonable, the count himself I mean. The Razumóvskis wanted to buy his house and his estate near Moscow, but it drags on and on. He asks too much.”

cases.sentence: — ___, но очень pauvre sire.[658] плох.
cases.explain: «Добрый старик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “A kindly old man but not up to much. And why do they stay on so long in Moscow? They meant to leave for the country long ago. Natáli is quite well again now, isn’t she?” Julie asked Pierre with a knowing smile.

cases.sentence: — Они ждут ___, — сказал Пьер.
cases.explain: «меньшого сына» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “They are waiting for their younger son,” Pierre replied. “He joined Obolénski’s Cossacks and went to Bélaya Tsérkov where the regiment is being formed. But now they have had him transferred to my regiment and are expecting him every day. The count wanted to leave long ago, but the countess won’t on any account leave Moscow till her son returns.”

cases.sentence: — Я их ___ видела у Архаровых.
cases.explain: «третьего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I met them the day before yesterday at the Arkhárovs’. Natáli has recovered her looks and is brighter. She sang a song. How easily some people get over everything!”

cases.sentence: — Ну, полноте, ___, c'est la fable de tout Moscou. Je vous admire, ma parole d’honneur.[660] это вся Москва знает.
cases.explain: «милый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, come, my dear count! C’est la fable de tout Moscou. Je vous admire, ma parole d’honneur!”88

cases.sentence: — Non, madame,[663] Нет, сударыня, — продолжал Пьер ___.
cases.explain: «недовольным тоном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “No, madame!” Pierre continued in a tone of displeasure, “I have not taken on myself the role of Natálya Rostóva’s knight at all, and have not been to their house for nearly a month. But I cannot understand the cruelty …”

cases.sentence: — Qui s’excuse — s’accuse,[664] Кто извиняется, тот обвиняет себя, — улыбаясь и махая корпией, говорила Жюли, и, чтобы за ней осталось ___, сейчас же переменила разговор.
cases.explain: «последнее слово» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Qui s’excuse s’accuse,”89 said Julie, smiling and waving the lint triumphantly, and to have the last word she promptly changed the subject. “Do you know what I heard today? Poor Márie Bolkónskaya arrived in Moscow yesterday. Do you know that she has lost her father?”

cases.sentence: Это ___. Nicolas Ростов.
cases.explain: «целый роман» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “She is well, but sad. But do you know who rescued her? It is quite a romance. Nicolas Rostóv! She was surrounded, and they wanted to kill her and had wounded some of her people. He rushed in and saved her. …”

cases.sentence: — Решительно, это ___ сделано, чтобы все старые невесты шли замуж. Catiche одна, княжна Болконская другая.
cases.explain: «общее бегство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Another romance,” said the militia officer. “Really, this general flight has been arranged to get all the old maids married off. Catiche is one and Princess Bolkónskaya another.”

cases.sentence: — Решительно, это общее бегство сделано, чтобы все ___ шли замуж. Catiche одна, княжна Болконская другая.
cases.explain: «старые невесты» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Another romance,” said the militia officer. “Really, this general flight has been arranged to get all the old maids married off. Catiche is one and Princess Bolkónskaya another.”

cases.sentence: — Вы знаете, что я в ___ думаю, что она un petit peu amoureuse du jeune homme.[665] немножечко влюблена в молодого человека.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Do you know, I really believe she is un petit peu amoureuse du jeune homme.”90

cases.sentence: — Вы знаете, что я в самом деле думаю, что она un petit peu amoureuse du jeune homme.[665] немножечко влюблена в ___.
cases.explain: «молодого человека» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Do you know, I really believe she is un petit peu amoureuse du jeune homme.”90
